```text
---
# =============================================================================
# gui_apps_linux — Ubuntu/Debian desktop GUI app installer
#
# Handles the "desktop-only" category of apps that aren't in the apt default
# repos: Alacritty (cargo), AppImageLauncher (PPA / .deb / Lite), VSCode
# (Microsoft apt repo), Cursor (.deb with graceful fallback), libfuse2
# (AppImage runtime on Ubuntu 22.04+), and a placeholder hook for Antigravity
# once an official Linux package ships.
#
# No-op on:
#   - macOS  → Brewfile (`cask "alacritty"`, `cask "visual-studio-code"` when
#              you add them) covers the desktop story. This role emits a
#              debug note only on Darwin, no install logic runs.
#   - armhf  → 32-bit ARM has no practical GUI story; cargo builds are slow
#              and AppImages lack first-class armv7 support.
#   - noRoot → `--skip-tags sudo` (set by run_onchange) skips every system
#              apt/deb/PPA task. AppImageLauncher Lite (user-level AppImage)
#              still runs when `gui_apps_linux_no_root=true` is passed via
#              `--extra-vars`.
#
# Editor user-config overlays (settings.json / keybindings.json) are handled
# by chezmoi itself, NOT ansible — see `.chezmoitemplates/editor/` and the
# `modify_settings.json.tmpl` / `create_keybindings.json.tmpl` source files.
# =============================================================================

# --- Platform banner ---

- name: Announce gui_apps_linux is Linux-only (macOS uses Brewfile)
  when: ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Darwin'
  ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: >-
      gui_apps_linux is Linux-only. macOS GUI apps are declared in
      dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl (alacritty cask, etc.).

- name: Skip gui_apps_linux on armhf
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
    - target_architecture == 'armv7l'
  ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: >-
      Skipping gui_apps_linux on armhf — no practical GUI stack,
      cargo builds of alacritty are very slow, and upstream AppImages
      do not target armv7.

# =============================================================================
# Alacritty (moved verbatim from the former alacritty role)
# =============================================================================

- name: Install Alacritty build dependencies
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
    - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name:
      - cmake
      - pkg-config
      - libfontconfig1-dev
      - libxcb-xfixes0-dev
      - libxkbcommon-dev
    state: present
    update_cache: false

- name: Check if Alacritty is already installed
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
    - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
  ansible.builtin.command: alacritty --version
  register: alacritty_check
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
  environment:
    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.cargo/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"

- name: Install Alacritty via cargo
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
    - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
    - alacritty_check.rc != 0
  ansible.builtin.command: cargo install alacritty
  args:
    creates: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.cargo/bin/alacritty"
  environment:
    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/share/mise/shims:{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.cargo/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"
  timeout: 3600

- name: Ensure user icon + application dirs exist
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
    - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
  ansible.builtin.file:
    path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/{{ item }}"
    state: directory
    mode: '0755'
  loop:
    - .local/share/icons/hicolor/scalable/apps
    - .local/share/applications

- name: Download Alacritty SVG icon
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
    - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
  ansible.builtin.get_url:
    url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alacritty/alacritty/master/extra/logo/alacritty-term.svg
    dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/share/icons/hicolor/scalable/apps/alacritty.svg"
    mode: '0644'
  retries: 3
  delay: 5

- name: Install Alacritty .desktop entry
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
    - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
  ansible.builtin.copy:
    dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/share/applications/alacritty.desktop"
    mode: '0644'
    content: |
      [Desktop Entry]
      Type=Application
      TryExec=alacritty
      Exec=alacritty
      Icon=alacritty
      Terminal=false
      Categories=System;TerminalEmulator;
      Name=Alacritty
      GenericName=Terminal
      Comment=A fast, cross-platform, OpenGL terminal emulator
      StartupWMClass=alacritty

- name: Refresh desktop application database
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
    - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
  ansible.builtin.command: update-desktop-database "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/share/applications"
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

# =============================================================================
# libfuse2 — AppImage runtime on Ubuntu 22.04+
# Ubuntu dropped libfuse2 from the default install around 22.04; AppImages
# compiled against it fail with a cryptic "dlopen(): error loading libfuse.so.2"
# on boot. Installing the compat package fixes every AppImage we ship below.
# =============================================================================

- name: Install libfuse2 for AppImage compatibility
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
    - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name: libfuse2
    state: present
    update_cache: false
  ignore_errors: true

# =============================================================================
# AppImageLauncher — desktop integration for AppImages
#
# Strategy (in order):
#   1. PPA `ppa:appimagelauncher-team/stable` — preferred on 20.04/22.04.
#   2. GitHub `.deb` fallback — PPA is known-broken on Ubuntu 24.04 "noble"
#      as of 2026 (upstream has not published a noble release); the latest
#      GitHub `.deb` still installs cleanly.
#   3. AppImageLauncher **Lite** — a user-level AppImage that integrates
#      itself without root. Enabled when `gui_apps_linux_no_root=true`.
#
# Docs: see docs/tools/appimage.md for install paths, ail-cli usage, and
# the libfuse2 / AppArmor gotchas on recent Ubuntu.
# =============================================================================

- name: Check if AppImageLauncher is installed (system-wide)
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
    - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
  ansible.builtin.command: dpkg -s appimagelauncher
  register: ail_check
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

- name: Install AppImageLauncher via PPA
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
    - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
    - not (gui_apps_linux_no_root | bool)
    - ail_check.rc != 0
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  block:
    - name: Add AppImageLauncher PPA
      ansible.builtin.apt_repository:
        repo: ppa:appimagelauncher-team/stable
        state: present
        update_cache: true
        filename: appimagelauncher-team-stable
      ignore_errors: true
      register: ail_ppa

    - name: Install appimagelauncher from PPA
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        name: appimagelauncher
        state: present
      when: ail_ppa is succeeded
      register: ail_apt_install
      ignore_errors: true
  rescue:
    - name: Warn AppImageLauncher PPA install failed
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "AppImageLauncher PPA install failed — trying GitHub .deb fallback next."

- name: Install AppImageLauncher from GitHub .deb (fallback)
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'aarch64']
    - not (gui_apps_linux_no_root | bool)
    - ail_check.rc != 0
    - (ail_apt_install is not defined) or (ail_apt_install is not succeeded)
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  block:
    - name: Get latest AppImageLauncher release metadata
      ansible.builtin.uri:
        url: https://api.github.com/repos/TheAssassin/AppImageLauncher/releases/latest
        return_content: true
      register: ail_release

    - name: Resolve AppImageLauncher .deb asset URL
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        ail_deb_url: >-
          {{ (ail_release.json.assets
              | selectattr('name', 'match', '^appimagelauncher_.*_' + ail_deb_arch + '\\.deb$')
              | map(attribute='browser_download_url')
              | list
              | first) | default('') }}
      vars:
        ail_deb_arch: "{{ {'x86_64': 'amd64', 'aarch64': 'arm64'}[target_architecture] }}"

    - name: Download AppImageLauncher .deb
      when: ail_deb_url | length > 0
      ansible.builtin.get_url:
        url: "{{ ail_deb_url }}"
        dest: /tmp/appimagelauncher.deb
        mode: '0644'
        timeout: 180

    - name: Install AppImageLauncher .deb
      when: ail_deb_url | length > 0
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        deb: /tmp/appimagelauncher.deb
        state: present
  rescue:
    - name: Warn AppImageLauncher .deb install failed
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "AppImageLauncher .deb install failed — the Lite user-level variant is still available via noRoot mode."

- name: Install AppImageLauncher Lite (user-level, noRoot)
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'aarch64']
    - gui_apps_linux_no_root | bool
  block:
    - name: Ensure ~/Applications exists
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/Applications"
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    - name: Get latest AppImageLauncher release (for Lite variant)
      ansible.builtin.uri:
        url: https://api.github.com/repos/TheAssassin/AppImageLauncher/releases/latest
        return_content: true
      register: ail_lite_release

    - name: Resolve AppImageLauncher Lite AppImage URL
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        ail_lite_url: >-
          {{ (ail_lite_release.json.assets
              | selectattr('name', 'match', '^appimagelauncher-lite-.*-' + target_architecture + '\\.AppImage$')
              | map(attribute='browser_download_url')
              | list
              | first) | default('') }}

    - name: Download AppImageLauncher Lite
      when: ail_lite_url | length > 0
      ansible.builtin.get_url:
        url: "{{ ail_lite_url }}"
        dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/Applications/appimagelauncher-lite.AppImage"
        mode: '0755'
        timeout: 180
      register: ail_lite_dl
      ignore_errors: true

    - name: Note how to finalise AppImageLauncher Lite integration
      when: ail_lite_dl is defined and ail_lite_dl is succeeded
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: >-
          Downloaded AppImageLauncher Lite to ~/Applications/appimagelauncher-lite.AppImage.
          Run `~/Applications/appimagelauncher-lite.AppImage install` once to register
          the integration; see docs/tools/appimage.md for ail-cli usage.

# =============================================================================
# Visual Studio Code — official Microsoft apt repository
# =============================================================================

- name: Check if VSCode is installed
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
    - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
  ansible.builtin.command: dpkg -s code
  register: vscode_check
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

- name: Install VSCode via Microsoft apt repo
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'aarch64']
    - not (gui_apps_linux_no_root | bool)
    - vscode_check.rc != 0
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  block:
    - name: Ensure /etc/apt/keyrings exists
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: /etc/apt/keyrings
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    - name: Add Microsoft GPG key (dearmored)
      ansible.builtin.shell: |
        set -eu
        wget -qO- https://packages.microsoft.com/keys/microsoft.asc \
          | gpg --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg
      args:
        creates: /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg

    - name: Add VSCode apt repository
      ansible.builtin.apt_repository:
        repo: >-
          deb [arch={{ {'x86_64': 'amd64', 'aarch64': 'arm64'}[target_architecture] }}
          signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg]
          https://packages.microsoft.com/repos/code stable main
        state: present
        filename: vscode
        update_cache: true

    - name: Install VSCode package
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        name: code
        state: present
  rescue:
    - name: Warn VSCode install failed
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "VSCode install failed — rerun with --tags gui_apps after fixing network/GPG/apt issues."

# =============================================================================
# Cursor — .deb from cursor.com
#
# The download API returns a redirect to the latest build for the given
# platform. The whole block is tolerant: a failed download is logged but
# does not fail the playbook. Users can always fall back to the AppImage
# path documented in docs/tools/appimage.md.
# =============================================================================

- name: Check if Cursor is installed
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
    - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
  ansible.builtin.command: dpkg -s cursor
  register: cursor_check
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

- name: Install Cursor via .deb
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'aarch64']
    - not (gui_apps_linux_no_root | bool)
    - cursor_check.rc != 0
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  block:
    - name: Download latest Cursor .deb (redirect from cursor.com)
      ansible.builtin.get_url:
        url: >-
          https://cursor.com/api/download?platform=linux-{{
            {'x86_64': 'x64', 'aarch64': 'arm64'}[target_architecture]
          }}&releaseTrack=stable
        dest: /tmp/cursor.deb
        mode: '0644'
        timeout: 300
        follow: true
      register: cursor_dl
      ignore_errors: true

    - name: Install Cursor .deb
      when: cursor_dl is defined and cursor_dl is succeeded
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        deb: /tmp/cursor.deb
        state: present
      ignore_errors: true
  rescue:
    - name: Warn Cursor .deb install failed
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: >-
          Cursor .deb install failed. You can fall back to the AppImage flow —
          download from https://cursor.com/download and drop it under
          ~/Applications/; AppImageLauncher will auto-integrate. See
          docs/tools/appimage.md for the full recipe.

# =============================================================================
# Antigravity (placeholder)
# No official Linux build at the time of writing; leave the hook disabled so
# the structure is obvious when upstream starts shipping a .deb or AppImage.
# =============================================================================

- name: Antigravity Linux install (disabled — no official Linux build yet)
  when: false
  ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: >-
      TODO: when an official Antigravity Linux .deb or AppImage ships,
      add install tasks here mirroring the Cursor block above.
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-04-24 13:42:59Z)**_

確認現狀：

- **macOS**：有裝 Arc — `dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl` 裡 `cask "arc"` 是啟用的（同區塊還有 `# cask "google-chrome"` / `# cask "tor-browser"` 被註解掉）。
- **Ubuntu Desktop**：完全沒裝任何瀏覽器。`dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml` 只處理 Alacritty、AppImageLauncher、libfuse2、VSCode、Cursor，沒有 Zen 或其他 browser。

要加 Zen 到 Ubuntu Desktop 的話，建議走 **官方 tarball + 自建 .desktop entry**（不是 AppImage）：

- Zen 官方 Linux 分發只有 tarball（`.tar.xz` for x86_64 / aarch64）和 Flatpak，**沒有 AppImage**。
- Tarball 解到 `~/.local/share/zen/`，shim 連到 `~/.local/bin/zen`，desktop entry 寫到 `~/.local/share/applications/zen.desktop` — 跟現有 Alacritty 區塊的模式一致（icon + .desktop + `update-desktop-database`）。
- 好處：純 user-level、`noRoot` 模式也能跑；升級走 `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`（符合 install-only invariant）。
- 缺點：要自己處理版本檢查（GitHub releases API → `zen-browser/desktop`），不像 apt repo 自動更新。

順便問：macOS 那邊也想加嗎？`brew install --cask zen` 是可用的，可以一起補進 Brewfile.darwin.tmpl 跟 Arc 並列。

要我直接動手就說一聲，會：
1. 在 `gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml` 加 Zen 區塊（tarball + shim + .desktop）
2. （可選）Brewfile 加 `cask "zen"`
3. 在 `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` 加 `upgrade_zen` 函式
4. 更新 `README.md` 跟 `docs/` 對應頁

```text
13:## Architecture
112:| `installCodingAgents` | true | Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, RTK, td, sidecar, specify-cli, etc. |
117:| `installBrewApps` | false | General GUI apps via Homebrew Brewfile (terminals, browsers, utilities, mas; excludes AI desktop apps) |
141:- `~/.condarc` - Conda/Mamba channels with TUNA Anaconda mirror (only managed when `useChineseMirror=true`, preserves `auto_activate_base`/user channel prefs)
146:- `~/.config/alacritty/` - Alacritty terminal config (CSI-u keybindings for `Ctrl+Number` tmux window switching, `option_as_alt` for Meta keys)
147:- `~/Library/Application Support/{Code,Cursor,Antigravity}/User/` (macOS) + `~/.config/{Code,Cursor,Antigravity}/User/` (Linux) - Editor settings overlay: `modify_settings.json` deep-merges a 6-key baseline (Hack Nerd Font Mono, relative line numbers, format on save, smart-accept suggestion, terminal font) into each editor's live `settings.json` without overwriting other keys; `create_keybindings.json` seeds 5 universal keybindings on a fresh machine and never overwrites editor-added entries. Canonical templates live under [`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`](.chezmoitemplates/editor/); `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` gates each editor dir with a `stat` presence check so uninstalled editors never produce phantom directories.
155:- `~/.cursor/cli-config.json`, `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml` - Coding-agent CLI overlays: each `modify_*` script deep-merges a small managed baseline (preferences, features, curated plugins) into the CLI's live config, preserving auth tokens, per-project trust, sessions, and other machine-local state. Codex specifically round-trips `[projects]` and `[marketplaces.*]` so per-project trust paths never get clobbered. OpenCode legacy `~/.config/opencode/config.json` is migrated to the modern filename by a one-shot `run_once_before_50_opencode_migrate.sh.tmpl`. Full design: [docs/tools/agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md).
157:- `~/.tmux.conf` - Tmux configuration with TPM plugins (resurrect, continuum, tmux-floax floating pane, tmux-fzf for fuzzy keybinding/session/pane search rebound to `prefix+?`, tmux-fzf-url, tmux-open), vim-style copy mode with clipboard yank, capture-pane helpers (`prefix+y`/`Y`/`C-y`), a native popup menu (`prefix+Space` or `prefix+e`, script-driven with submenus and height-aware trimming) with layout/resize/session management, popup shell (`prefix+\``) and lazygit popup (`prefix+G`), a glow-rendered cheatsheet (`prefix+Space` → `?`), vim-style pane nav, `Ctrl+1..9` quick window switching (CSI-u terminals), extended-keys for coding agents (including `Ctrl+/` in Neovim), sesh keybindings (`prefix+g` fzf picker, `prefix+T` television picker, `prefix+O` built-in picker, `prefix+W` window picker, `prefix+S` last), responsive Catppuccin status bar (adapts modules to terminal width for mobile), and config reload on `prefix+R` ([docs](docs/tools/tmux/README.md))
171:- `~/.config/television/cable/skills.toml` + `~/.config/television/cable/skills-walk.toml` - Two Television channels for browsing agent skills: `skills` parses `npx skills list` (project + global, with Agents column), `skills-walk` walks `~/.agents/`, `~/.claude/`, `~/.codex/`, `~/.cursor/skills-cursor/` directly without invoking npx; both preview SKILL.md with bat
172:- `~/.config/television/cable/agent-sessions.toml` + `~/.config/television/agent-sessions.py` - Unified Television channel for coding-agent sessions across OpenCode (SQLite), Claude Code (JSONL), Codex (JSONL), Cursor Agent CLI (store.db), and Cursor IDE composer chats (state.vscdb); 6 source cycles (all/per-agent), content-searchable via first-user-message snippet, `Enter` prints `cd <dir> && <agent> --resume <id>`, `Alt+T` resumes in current shell (Cursor IDE: opens workspace folder via `cursor <dir>` since IDE has no chat-resume CLI flag)
222:- **Coding Agents** (optional): Claude Code, `claude-hud` statusline plugin, Codex CLI, CodexBar, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, RTK, SpecStory, OpenChamber, td, sidecar, specify-cli
230:- **GUI Apps** (macOS): general terminals, editors, browsers, network tools, and utilities via Brewfile when `installBrewApps=true`, including developer apps like `dbeaver-community` and `superset` (Apple Silicon only); AI desktop apps via Brewfile when `installAiDesktopApps=true` (`claude`, `chatgpt`, `opencode-desktop`, `antigravity`, `codex-app` on Apple Silicon only, `codeisland` notch HUD for coding-agent activity, and `ollama-app` only when `installLlmTools=true`); Tailscale Desktop via Mac App Store `mas`, avoids pkg sudo prompt; Tailscale CLI via `brew "tailscale"` in shared Brewfile
239:- **GUI Apps on Linux** (`gui_apps` tag on `ubuntu_desktop`): [`gui_apps_linux`](dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml) bundles Alacritty (cargo), AppImageLauncher (PPA with `.deb` fallback, Lite variant for noRoot), VSCode (Microsoft apt repo), Cursor (`.deb`), and `libfuse2` for AppImage compatibility. macOS equivalents ship via [`Brewfile.darwin.tmpl`](dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl). See [docs/tools/appimage.md](docs/tools/appimage.md) for AppImageLauncher install paths, `ail-cli` usage, and Ubuntu 24.04 AppArmor gotchas.
```

```text
1:# AppImage & AppImageLauncher on Ubuntu
3:[AppImage](https://appimage.org/) is a single-file app format for Linux: download, `chmod +x`, run. No root, no install step, no dependencies beyond the host's `libc` and `libfuse2`. The format is how Cursor, Obsidian, Joplin, Bitwarden Desktop, and many AI / markdown / media tools ship their Linux builds.
5:The gap is desktop integration: a bare `~/Applications/foo.AppImage` doesn't show up in the GNOME/KDE launcher, has no `.desktop` entry, and doesn't get picked up by `xdg-open`. That's where **[AppImageLauncher](https://github.com/TheAssassin/AppImageLauncher)** comes in — a system daemon that watches a directory for AppImages and auto-integrates them (icon extraction, `.desktop` generation, optional move into a canonical location, optional update-via-delta).
7:This repo installs AppImageLauncher on `ubuntu_desktop` machines via the [`gui_apps_linux`](../../dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml) Ansible role. This doc covers the *why*, the three install paths, and the two footguns you'll hit on current Ubuntu.
9:## Why AppImageLauncher vs bare AppImages vs `appimaged`
15:| **AppImageLauncher** (this repo) | Yes | Yes (opt-in) | Yes (Lite) | First-run modal asks "Integrate or Run once?", stores integrated AppImages in `~/Applications/`, handles removal cleanly. |
17:The **first-run prompt** is the real win: double-click an AppImage and AppImageLauncher asks whether to install it system-wide (move to `~/Applications/`, generate `.desktop` + icon + MIME handlers) or run once and delete. Makes AppImages feel like regular apps without locking you into yet another store.
35:The PPA [has no release for Ubuntu 24.04](https://github.com/TheAssassin/AppImageLauncher/issues) as of 2026; maintainership has stalled. The latest `.deb` from the GitHub releases page still installs cleanly on noble:
39:curl -fsSL "https://api.github.com/repos/TheAssassin/AppImageLauncher/releases/latest" \
40:  | jq -r --arg a "$ARCH" '.assets[] | select(.name | test("^appimagelauncher_.*_\($a)\\.deb$")).browser_download_url' \
47:### 3. AppImageLauncher **Lite** (no root, user-level)
49:Lite is AppImageLauncher shipped as an AppImage itself — integrates itself into `~/.config/autostart`, `~/.local/share/applications`, `~/.local/share/icons`. Useful on locked-down machines where you can't `sudo`.
53:curl -fsSL "https://api.github.com/repos/TheAssassin/AppImageLauncher/releases/latest" \
54:  | jq -r --arg a "$(uname -m)" '.assets[] | select(.name | test("^appimagelauncher-lite-.*-\($a)\\.AppImage$")).browser_download_url' \
60:The Ansible role runs this when `gui_apps_linux_no_root=true` is passed (automatically set by `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl` in the `noRoot` chezmoi profile).
67:ail-cli integrate ~/Applications/Cursor.AppImage
69:ail-cli deintegrate ~/Applications/Cursor.AppImage
76:### Cursor (when the `.deb` install misbehaves)
78:The [`gui_apps_linux`](../../dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml) role installs Cursor via the official `.deb` from `cursor.com/api/download?platform=linux-x64`. If that URL ever changes or returns a broken package, the manual AppImage flow is:
83:mv ~/Downloads/Cursor-*.AppImage ~/Applications/Cursor.AppImage
84:chmod +x ~/Applications/Cursor.AppImage
85:ail-cli integrate ~/Applications/Cursor.AppImage
89:Editor user settings (`settings.json`, `keybindings.json`) are independent of install method — chezmoi manages them via [`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`](../../.chezmoitemplates/editor/) regardless of whether Cursor came from `.deb` or AppImage.
93:Same pattern: drop AppImage in `~/Applications/`, integrate with `ail-cli` or the first-run prompt. These apps self-update via AppImage delta (AppImageLauncher handles the update prompt too).
116:Ubuntu 24.04 enabled the `unprivileged_userns_restriction` AppArmor profile, which breaks the Electron / Chromium sandbox inside AppImages (Cursor, VSCode, Obsidian, any Chromium-based tool). Symptom: the app window never appears, logs show `SUID sandbox helper binary was found, but is not configured correctly`.
123:   ~/Applications/Cursor.AppImage --no-sandbox
126:   For integrated apps, edit the generated `~/.local/share/applications/appimagekit-<hash>-Cursor.desktop` and append `--no-sandbox` to the `Exec=` line.
140:AppImageLauncher names integrated desktop files `appimagekit-<hash>-<name>.desktop`, with `<hash>` derived from the AppImage binary. Updating an AppImage in-place (e.g. via its own updater) leaves a stale hash. Fix:
150:- [`dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml) — the install role
151:- [`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`](../../.chezmoitemplates/editor/) — editor settings overlay that lands inside Cursor/VSCode/Antigravity regardless of install method
```
</details></tool-use>

73	
74	## Recipes
75	
76	### Cursor (when the `.deb` install misbehaves)
77	
78	The [`gui_apps_linux`](../../dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml) role installs Cursor via the official `.deb` from `cursor.com/api/download?platform=linux-x64`. If that URL ever changes or returns a broken package, the manual AppImage flow is:
79	
80	```bash
81	mkdir -p ~/Applications
82	# Download the latest AppImage from https://cursor.com/download ("Download AppImage" link)
83	mv ~/Downloads/Cursor-*.AppImage ~/Applications/Cursor.AppImage
84	chmod +x ~/Applications/Cursor.AppImage
85	ail-cli integrate ~/Applications/Cursor.AppImage
86	# (or double-click to trigger the first-run prompt)
87	```
88	
89	Editor user settings (`settings.json`, `keybindings.json`) are independent of install method — chezmoi manages them via [`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`](../../.chezmoitemplates/editor/) regardless of whether Cursor came from `.deb` or AppImage.
90	
91	### Obsidian / Bitwarden Desktop / Joplin
92	
93	Same pattern: drop AppImage in `~/Applications/`, integrate with `ail-cli` or the first-run prompt. These apps self-update via AppImage delta (AppImageLauncher handles the update prompt too).
94	
95	## Troubleshooting
96	
97	### `libfuse.so.2: cannot open shared object file`
98	
99	Ubuntu 22.04+ dropped `libfuse2` from the default install. AppImages compiled against fuse 2 fail with:
100	
101	```plain
102	dlopen(): error loading libfuse.so.2
103	AppImages require FUSE to run.
104	```
105	
106	Fix:
107
